column2: On the authority of Abū Dharr al-Ghifārī (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet ﷺ, in what he relates from his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, that He said:

“O My servants, I have forbidden injustice for Myself and have made it forbidden among you, so do not wrong one another. O My servants, all of you are astray except those I have guided, so seek guidance from Me and I will guide you. O My servants, all of you are hungry except those I have fed, so seek food from Me and I will feed you.

O My servants, all of you are naked except those I have clothed, so seek clothing from Me and I will clothe you. O My servants, you err by night and by day, and I forgive all sins, so seek My forgiveness and I will forgive you.

O My servants, you will never attain the power to harm Me so as to harm Me, nor attain the power to benefit Me so as to benefit Me. O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were as pious as the most pious heart of any one man among you, that would not increase My dominion in anything.
O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were as wicked as the most wicked heart of any one man among you, that would not decrease My dominion in anything.

O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were to stand together on one plain and ask of Me, and I gave each one what he asked, that would not decrease what I have except as much as a needle decreases [the sea] when it is dipped into the sea.

O My servants, it is only your deeds that I record for you and then repay you for in full. So whoever finds good, let him praise Allah; and whoever finds otherwise, let him blame no one but himself.” Reported by Muslim.

Ḥarramtu (“I have forbidden”): I have prohibited. Al-ẓulm (“injustice”): putting a thing in other than its proper place. “For Myself”: out of His favour and kindness. “And have made it forbidden among you”: I have ruled that it is forbidden to you. “So do not wrong one another”: let none of you wrong another.

“All of you are astray”: from the path of truth, if left [to yourselves]. “Except those I have guided”: whom I have enabled to carry out the commands and avoid the prohibitions. “So seek guidance from Me”: ask Me for guidance. “I will guide you”: I will enable you to it. “I forgive sins”: I cover them and erase them.
Tukhṭiʾūna (“you err”): you sin. “On one plain”: in one place. “So seek My forgiveness”: ask Me for forgiveness.

“I will forgive you”: I will erase your sins. Al-mikhyaṭ (“a needle”): the needle. Uḥṣīhā (“I record”): I preserve them. “Then repay you for in full”: I give you the recompense of your deeds in full. “Finds good”: reward. “And whoever finds otherwise”: evil.
“Let him blame no one but himself”: let him censure no one but his own soul, which commands evil.
The perfection of Allah the Exalted's justice and His being free of injustice, and that all His actions are justice and wisdom.
The printed text reads كمال فعل الله, evidently for كمال عدل الله (“the perfection of Allah's justice”), as the rest of the sentence shows.
The prohibition of injustice among the servants.
Drawing attention to creation's need of Allah the Exalted and their inability to attain their benefits and ward off their harms except by Allah the Exalted making it easy for them.
The dominion of Allah is utterly perfect: it is not increased by the obedience of creation nor decreased by their disobedience.
Piety and wickedness go back to the heart: when it is sound the limbs are sound, and when it is corrupt the limbs are corrupt.
The obligation to turn to Allah in everything that befalls the servant, asking Him for help and for success in what pleases Him.
The treasuries of Allah are full and never run out, since they have no end.
Allah preserves the deeds of His servants and records them for them and against them, then repays them in full on the Day of Resurrection.
All good is from Allah's favour to His servants, without any obligation or entitlement, and all evil is from the soul, desire and the devil.

This ḥadīth qudsī, which contains great benefits in the fundamentals, branches and manners of the religion, teaches us that Allah, Glorified is He, has forbidden injustice for Himself out of His favour and kindness to His servants, and has made injustice forbidden among His creation, so that no one wrongs another;

that all creation is astray from the path of truth except by Allah's guidance and enabling, and whoever asks Allah, He enables him and guides him; that creation is poor before Allah and in need of Him, and whoever asks Allah, He fulfils his need and suffices him;

that they sin by night and by day, and Allah the Exalted covers and overlooks when the servant asks for forgiveness; that however much they try with their words and deeds, they cannot harm Allah in anything or benefit Him;

that if they were as pious as the most pious heart of one man, or as wicked as the most wicked heart of one man, their piety would not increase Allah's dominion, nor would their wickedness decrease His dominion in anything, because they are weak and poor before Allah, needing Him in every situation,

time and place; that if they stood in one place asking Allah, and He gave each one what he asked, that would not decrease anything of what Allah has, because His treasuries, Glorified is He, are full and no spending diminishes them,

pouring out night and day; and that Allah preserves all the deeds of His servants and records them for them and against them, then repays them in full on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever finds the recompense of his deeds to be good,

let him praise Allah for enabling him to obey Him; and whoever finds the recompense of his deeds to be something else, let him blame no one but his own soul, which commands evil and led him to loss. We seek refuge with Allah from that. Among what has been said about this:
You have filled the record of the recording angels with sins; / if you forget them, your Lord knows.
Another poet:
The noble recording angels suffice as witnesses, / and the Lord of the worlds suffices as Witness.
And it has been said about injustice:
Never do wrong when you have the power to, / for wrongdoing at its source leads to regret.
Your eyes sleep while the wronged one is awake, / supplicating against you, and the eye of Allah does not sleep.
Another poet:
Do you mock supplication and scorn it? / What do you know of what supplication has done?
The arrows of the night strike home, but / they have a term, and every term comes to an end.
My Lord holds them back when He wills, / and releases them when the decree is fulfilled.
